title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
name: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Revise a scary probability using real reference points and opposing evidence.
steps:
1. Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations.
3. Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Act from the revision, not the original alarm.

win: Your second estimate differed from the alarm number because actual evidence had entered the calculation.

title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
name: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
goal: Loosen a thought's authority by changing how its voice sounds.
steps:
1. Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Then say it again in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
numberedSteps:
1. Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Then say it again in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
numbered_steps:
1. Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Then say it again in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
win: The same words felt more like a possibility once tone and confidence were altered.
mindBend: Your brain partly judges a thought by delivery. Certainty can be smuggled in through tone.
mind_bend: Your brain partly judges a thought by delivery. Certainty can be smuggled in through tone.
formulaFlow: Read Wrong → Keep Words → Natural Voice

title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
name: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
goal: Make a heavy thought visually smaller without arguing with its words.
steps:
1. Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move it two metres away.
4. Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.

title: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
name: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
goal: Return to what matters without turning a detour into a character trial.
steps:
1. State what moved off course in plain language.
2. Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.
numberedSteps:
1. State what moved off course in plain language.

4. Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.
numbered_steps:

2. Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.
win: One value-based move happened before you judged yourself or redesigned the whole plan.
mindBend: A lapse becomes identity evidence only when the mind adds a verdict; behaviour can restart without that sentence.
mind_bend: A lapse becomes identity evidence only when the mind adds a verdict; behaviour can restart without that sentence.

Address repeated harmful drift with accountability and support, not endless self-restarts.

title: FIVE SAFE SIGNALS

steps:

3. End on the sense that feels most trustworthy today.

title: DROP THE APPEAL
name: DROP THE APPEAL
goal: Stop arguing with the existence of what happened and respond to the reality that remains.
steps:
1. State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the protest and answer: ‘I can dislike this without denying that it happened.’
3. Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.

goal: Stop reopening the case and turn toward what is possible now.
steps:
1. Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
2. Name the refusal without criticism.
3. Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
4. Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.

title: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
name: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
goal: Put one genuinely reinforcing experience into real time and notice it while it happens.
steps:
1. Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’
numberedSteps:
1. Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’
numbered_steps:
1. Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.

3. While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.

win: The activity happened at a protected time and three details were actually registered.
mindBend: Pleasure can be under-recorded even when it occurs — attention helps the brain keep the receipt.
mind_bend: Pleasure can be under-recorded even when it occurs — attention helps the brain keep the receipt.

title: READ THE SIGNAL WITHOUT TURNING IT UP
name: READ THE SIGNAL WITHOUT TURNING IT UP
ritual_name: READ THE SIGNAL WITHOUT TURNING IT UP
goal: Describe one existing body sensation neutrally and stop after one sensible check.
steps:
1. Notice only a sensation already present and do not intensify it.
2. Check the room, recent activity, and any known medical information.
3. Describe the sensation with neutral words such as warm, tight, or moving.
4. Choose rest, ordinary movement, support, or medical advice as appropriate.
5. Stop after one check and avoid repeated body monitoring.
numberedSteps:
1. Notice only a sensation already present and do not intensify it.
2. Check the room, recent activity, and any known medical information.
3. Describe the sensation with neutral words such as warm, tight, or moving.
4. Choose rest, ordinary movement, support, or medical advice as appropriate.
5. Stop after one check and avoid repeated body monitoring.
numbered_steps:
1. Notice only a sensation already present and do not intensify it.
2. Check the room, recent activity, and any known medical information.
3. Describe the sensation with neutral words such as warm, tight, or moving.
4. Choose rest, ordinary movement, support, or medical advice as appropriate.
5. Stop after one check and avoid repeated body monitoring.
win: The sensation was named without amplification, and the next response matched context rather than repeated monitoring.
mindBend: Repeated checking can make one body feeling seem bigger. One sensible check gives you information without turning monitoring into the main event.
mind_bend: Repeated checking can make one body feeling seem bigger. One sensible check gives you information without turning monitoring into the main event.
formulaFlow: Notice Signal → Check Facts → Name Quality → Choose Response → End Check
formula_flow: Notice Signal → Check Facts → Name Quality → Choose Response → End Check
safety:
PAUSE
Do not deliberately trigger, intensify, or test feared body sensations. Use this content only as non-exposure education unless a qualified clinician has assessed and supervised an exposure plan. Seek medical advice for uncertain symptoms.
This is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

title: DESIGN THE SURPRISE
name: DESIGN THE SURPRISE
goal: Test the feared prediction directly and keep whatever reality does not fit.
steps:
1. Picture the strongest testable prediction in visible terms.
2. Build a safe practice round aimed at that exact claim, not merely at feeling anxious.
3. Afterward, keep the original prediction, what occurred, and what the old model cannot easily explain.
numberedSteps:
1. Picture the strongest testable prediction in visible terms.
2. Build a safe practice round aimed at that exact claim, not merely at feeling anxious.
3. Afterward, keep the original prediction, what occurred, and what the old model cannot easily explain.
numbered_steps:
1. Picture the strongest testable prediction in visible terms.
2. Build a safe practice round aimed at that exact claim, not merely at feeling anxious.
3. Afterward, keep the original prediction, what occurred, and what the old model cannot easily explain.
win: The practice produced a visible result that could be compared with the original prediction instead of just anxiety level.
mindBend: A fear model changes fastest when reality produces a surprise it cannot easily explain away.
mind_bend: A fear model changes fastest when reality produces a surprise it cannot easily explain away.
formulaFlow: Picture Strongest → Build Safe → Picture Outcome
formula_flow: Picture Strongest → Build Safe → Picture Outcome

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: Move attention between body tension and steadiness without getting trapped in either.

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
name: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
ritual_name: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Let the body give a whole-picture response before analysis takes over.
steps:
1. Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave the answer unpolished.

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
name: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: Let a safe defensive impulse finish in miniature instead of freezing halfway.
steps:
1. Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe whether the body receives an ending.
numberedSteps:
1. Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe whether the body receives an ending.

1. Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.

about 1 minute

GOAL
Let a safe defensive impulse finish in miniature instead of freezing halfway.

A tiny push, turn, step, shield, or no reached a natural endpoint and returned to neutral.

An unfinished defence can keep feeling current. A small completed movement may give the body the ending the original impulse never reached.

name: CATCH THE RECOVERY SIGNAL
goal: Notice the first real sign that body alarm is already beginning to recover.
steps:
1. After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release.

4. Teach the mind what recovery looks like.

title: CLOSE THE SCAN, OPEN THE ROOM
name: CLOSE THE SCAN, OPEN THE ROOM
ritual_name: CLOSE THE SCAN, OPEN THE ROOM
goal: Stop scanning inward and reopen attention to the ordinary room around you.
steps:
1. Stop searching the body for remaining danger signals.
2. Widen your gaze until both sides of the room are visible.
3. Name two neutral sounds without judging what they mean.
4. Touch a safe ordinary texture and describe its surface.
5. Choose a simple external task that does not involve the memory.
numberedSteps:
1. Stop searching the body for remaining danger signals.
2. Widen your gaze until both sides of the room are visible.
3. Name two neutral sounds without judging what they mean.
4. Touch a safe ordinary texture and describe its surface.
5. Choose a simple external task that does not involve the memory.
numbered_steps:
1. Stop searching the body for remaining danger signals.
2. Widen your gaze until both sides of the room are visible.
3. Name two neutral sounds without judging what they mean.
4. Touch a safe ordinary texture and describe its surface.
5. Choose a simple external task that does not involve the memory.
win: Your gaze widened, neutral sounds and texture registered, and an external task replaced the body search.
mindBend: Repeated danger-checking can keep the alarm central. Widening outward gives the brain competing evidence about where you are.

formulaFlow: End Search → Open Field → Name Sounds → Touch Texture → Choose Task

safety:
PAUSE

title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
name: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Find which half of breathing is working too hard and ease only that side.
steps:
1. Observe three ordinary cycles.
2. Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
3. Which phase is working too hard.
4. Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
5. Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.

title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
name: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
goal: Alternate nostrils gently without holding, forcing, or chasing a special state.
steps:
1. Sit comfortably.
2. Without force, close one nostril and breathe through the other; switch sides for the next gentle cycle.
3. Continue alternating with an unhurried hand.
4. Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
5. Finish with both sides open and let breathing return to normal.

title: VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT
name: VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT
goal: Use a soft hum on the exhale and stop while it still feels kind.
steps:
1. Take an ordinary inhale.
2. Hum at a soft, comfortable pitch as air leaves, feeling vibration in lips, face, or chest.
3. Stop before empty.
4. Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind.

title: THE RETURN REP
name: THE RETURN REP
goal: Count honest returns of attention instead of demanding unbroken focus.
steps:
1. Select one neutral anchor.
2. Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
3. Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
4. Finish after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.

title: LET DARKNESS BE COMPLETE
name: LET DARKNESS BE COMPLETE
goal: Look at darkness as a visual field without filling it with imagined shapes.
steps:

2. When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field.
3. Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose.

title: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
name: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
goal: Stay with one thought until it naturally changes or disappears.
steps:
1. Select one naturally occurring thought.
2. Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
3. Spot the first instant when no trace can be found.
4. Do not resurrect it to verify the ending.
numberedSteps:

win: The thought reached a point where no trace was findable without being resurrected for checking.

title: THE RETURN CHAIN
name: THE RETURN CHAIN
goal: Build attention through a modest daily return instead of heroic sessions.
steps:
1. Choose one attentional act small enough to repeat daily.
2. Define its cue, duration, and one tiny restart signal.
3. Each session begins with the final second of yesterday’s intention: ‘return again.’ Protect repetition from heroic increases.
4. A chain is made of modest links.

title: RETURN THE OUTCOME
name: RETURN THE OUTCOME
goal: Do your part fully while releasing the result you cannot command.
steps:
1. Name the action within your responsibility.
2. Name the result you cannot command.
3. Offer the second to God, life, reality, community, or a principle larger than ego—using language authentic to you.
4. Then do the first with full care.
numberedSteps:

numbered_steps:
1. Name the action within your responsibility.
2. Name the result you cannot command.
3. Offer the second to God, life, reality, community, or a principle larger than ego—using language authentic to you.

win: Responsibility and outcome were separated, so effort could stay wholehearted without pretending control was total.
mindBend: Care and control are not the same resource. You can increase the first even where the second ends.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
name: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: Find the conditions under which a recurring pattern is weaker, then recreate one.
steps:
1. Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.

steps:

title: WORRY HAS OFFICE HOURS
name: WORRY HAS OFFICE HOURS
goal: Give worry a later appointment instead of letting it occupy the whole day.
steps:
1. Picture the worry exactly and schedule a specific review window later today.

3. At the appointment, decide: act, plan, accept, or discard.
4. Close on time even if certainty is absent.

title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
name: ROTATE THE CHAIR
goal: View the same event from your view, the other person’s possible view, a neutral view, and future-you.
steps:
1. Describe the event from your position.
2. Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
3. Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
4. Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
name: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Change which word carries the weight and notice how the sentence's meaning shifts.
steps:
1. Choose one short alarm sentence.
2. Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
name: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
goal: Give the loss a place while choosing what can still be carried forward.
steps:
1. Imagine a symbol, date, or place that represents what was lost.
2. Say what mattered and what you want to keep carrying forward.
3. Name what cannot continue.
4. Choose one value or memory you can carry without forcing closure.

title: MEANING ON HOLD
name: MEANING ON HOLD
goal: Delay meaning until facts from several channels are actually present.
steps:
1. Notice the event without explaining it.
2. Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
3. Until all three exist, name every meaning temporary.
4. Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.

title: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
name: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
goal: Lower one dominant memory channel while strengthening neutral present-day context.
steps:
1. Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell.
2. Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly.
3. At the same time, strengthen neutral present-day context: the room layout, today’s date, your clothing, or a distant sound.
numberedSteps:

win: Image, sound, touch, or smell softened slightly as today's room, date, clothing, or distant sound became stronger.

title: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
name: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
ritual_name: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
goal: Keep the specific lesson from a painful event without letting it become a verdict on your whole life.
steps:
1. Name the specific lesson the event genuinely supports.
2. Notice the global conclusion attached to it: ‘Nobody is safe,’ ‘I am weak,’ ‘Life is over,’ or another all-life verdict.
3. Ask whether the specific lesson still works without the global verdict. Keep what teaches; delete what condemns.

title: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
name: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
goal: Complete one safe defensive movement slowly, then return all effort to zero.
steps:
1. While safely seated, locate one area that still feels ready to push, brace, turn, or withdraw.
2. Choose a pain-free direction and add only light self-resistance.
3. Complete the movement slowly once, then release all effort rather than repeating it.
4. Compare resting pressure, movement range, and urge before and after.

plain:
FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Complete one safe defensive movement slowly, then return all effort to zero.

STEPS
1. While safely seated, locate one area that still feels ready to push, brace, turn, or withdraw.
2. Choose a pain-free direction and add only light self-resistance.
3. Complete the movement slowly once, then release all effort rather than repeating it.
4. Compare resting pressure, movement range, and urge before and after.

WIN
The body finished a single push, brace, turn, or withdrawal and could compare pressure, range, and urge afterward.

A body can stay prepared when a movement never receives a clear ending; one deliberate completion may create a full stop.

Find Readiness → Add Resistance → Complete Slowly → Check Neutral

Stop immediately with pain, dizziness, numbness, injury risk, or uncertain movement.

title: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
name: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
goal: Protect one active concern while giving the next item and the rest clear places to wait.
steps:
1. Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE.
2. Put only one concern in ACTIVE, one likely next item in WAITING, and mentally route everything else to ARCHIVE with a clear retrieval cue.
3. Give the active concern a protected time box.

title: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
name: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
ritual_name: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
goal: Use the mental mode that matches the actual demand instead of applying pressure with the wrong tool.
steps:
1. Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT.
2. Name the mode currently running.
3. Shut it down and do the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule.
numberedSteps:
1. Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT.
2. Name the mode currently running.
3. Shut it down and do the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule.
numbered_steps:
1. Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT.
2. Name the mode currently running.
3. Shut it down and do the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule.
win: Solve, decide, feel, accept, communicate, or wait was identified and the first matching action replaced the mismatched mode.
mindBend: More effort cannot fix a tool mismatch. Using the wrong mental operation creates friction that masquerades as difficulty.
mind_bend: More effort cannot fix a tool mismatch. Using the wrong mental operation creates friction that masquerades as difficulty.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Switch cleanly by saving context, completing one small piece, and defining the next action.

STEPS
1. Hold the loose context as one brief mental snapshot.
2. Choose this decision for now.
3. Begin a small piece you can complete now.
4. Set the required move as the next action.
5. Bring a clear restart point to mind.

WIN
The new task got a finished unit while the old context and future restart remained intact.

MIND BEND
Switching cost rises when both sides are unfinished. Even a tiny completion plus a saved handoff can reduce the cognitive tear.

FORMULA FLOW
Set Place → End Round → Start Small → Set Out → Save Place

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.

plain:
BRING IN A REALITY PARTNER

PLAY TIME
ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT

GOAL
Do not test reality alone and bring in a trusted person and qualified support.

STEPS
1. Stop testing the experience alone and avoid acting on unverified conclusions.
2. Contact a trusted person who can stay physically or verbally present.
3. Say, “I feel unsafe and need help checking what is real.”
4. Use the crisis or emergency options shown in the Safety box.
5. Stay connected until a qualified professional takes over.

WIN
You stayed connected to another person and urgent professional help took over the reality check.

Stay with a safe person and follow qualified support. Do not return to ordinary rituals.

title: THE NEW-INFORMATION TEST
name: THE NEW-INFORMATION TEST
goal: Test whether more analysis is adding information before giving it another round.
steps:
1. Notice whether this round of analysis has produced any genuinely new information.
2. Separate what happened from the role you are assigning yourself.
3. Set any extra work aside.
4. Check the first action against one immediate fact.
5. Reduce the remaining question to three words.

name: PROOF THROUGH ONE WINDOW
goal: Stop demanding final proof when the existing evidence is already enough to choose the next action.
steps:
1. State a single direct reality about the situation.
2. Pinpoint the final proof your mind is demanding.
3. Ask whether that proof would change the decision or only change the feeling of certainty.
4. Choose the next action using the evidence you already have.
5. Stop the review after that one decision.
